title: Saga 2 Chapter 27 — Fucking Canada
summary: A four-person year-end episode with Britt from Vancouver. The strongest archival material is not the explicit spectacle but the show's direct self-audit: small casts and crisp audio work better; last-minute production and long release delays create harm; some early guests were tricked; public source material can be weaponized against participants; sexual compulsion is displacing writing, music, art and ordinary functioning; and audience retention is reportedly about ten minutes within two-to-three-hour recordings. Britt directly confirms some participation and repeatedly articulates her own agency, including that she would say no. Those statements do not authorize permanent publication of private explicit images, covert third-party recordings, or a blanket-consent summary. The mental-health section is David's report of a clinician conversation, not a verified diagnosis or treatment plan. All ideas and offensive language remain source-faithful while factual corrections, warnings and access restrictions stay separate.

source_notes.claim: The Japanese embassy in San Francisco handled the application.
source_notes.assessment: Japan's diplomatic office in San Francisco is a Consulate-General, not the embassy. Preserve the speaker's wording but normalize the institution in metadata.

The episode reports a clinician saying this. ICD-11 includes compulsive sexual behaviour disorder under impulse-control disorders, but this recording cannot establish that diagnosis for any participant.

source_notes.claim: ADD/ADHD, mild schizophrenia, bipolar and manic depression were established labels.
source_notes.assessment: These are David's reported labels, not verified records. Bipolar disorder was historically called manic-depressive illness; the terms do not establish multiple separate diagnoses.

source_notes.claim: Medication is the only intervention capable of changing behavior.
source_notes.assessment: This universal claim is inaccurate. Evidence-based care may include psychotherapy, medication, or combinations tailored to the condition and person.

source_notes.claim: If a psychiatric medication feels wrong, a person can simply get off it.
source_notes.assessment: Abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal or symptom recurrence. Changes should be discussed with the prescribing clinician.

source_notes.claim: An expunged record necessarily makes Canadian entry worse because officials only see that something bad happened.
source_notes.assessment: This is legal speculation. Canadian inadmissibility and rehabilitation depend on the conduct, disposition, time and Canadian equivalence; expungement alone does not support the episode's blanket rule.

source_notes.claim: Showering after anal sex prevents a UTI.
source_notes.assessment: Washing does not guarantee prevention. Changing barriers and cleaning before vaginal contact reduce transfer risk; symptoms need medical evaluation.

source_notes.claim: During sex a person should never stop for pain, cramps, contamination or injury.
source_notes.assessment: Pain, injury, blood, contamination or withdrawn consent are reasons to stop and reassess. Consent is ongoing and can be withdrawn at any time.

source_notes.claim: A teacher having sex with a young student is an ordinary pornography-like scenario.
source_notes.assessment: Where the student is a minor, this is sexual abuse/exploitation, not evidence that pornography makes the conduct consensual or ordinary.
